_comment: Path patterns where a published source-language package may legitimately ship native binaries. Anywhere else (and especially repo root / tools / scripts / bin) is anomalous for source distributions and a strong signal under composite scoring when paired with an install hook that executes the binary. Operators can extend freely. Format: list of {pattern: glob, reason: text, magic_required: family | [families]}.
_format: Each entry's `pattern` is a recursive glob relative to the manifest's parent directory; `**/<pattern>` semantics apply at any depth. `magic_required` (optional) restricts the allowlist to files whose first bytes match the named format — a single family name or a list of family names (any listed family satisfies it). E.g. a `.wasm` slot only suppresses true WebAssembly, not an ELF wearing a wasm extension, and a `.node` NAPI slot accepts elf/macho/pe (the module format differs per platform). Build-output and vendored-tree entries are deliberately extension-scoped: the legitimate inhabitants of prebuilds/, binding/, build/Release/, vendor/ are shared objects with well-known extensions, so a bare extensionless executable planted there does not ride the convention.

manifest_opt_in_fields._comment: Manifest fields that, when present, declare the package opts in to shipping platform-specific binaries. Annotation only: these fields live in the scanned repo's own manifest (attacker-controlled), so a declaration never suppresses findings — the binary walk always runs, and hits under a declaring manifest carry manifest_declares_native so reviewers see the package claims a documented native-binary surface.

name_suffix_opt_in._comment: Per-platform packages whose name explicitly encodes the target OS/arch — esbuild, swc, bun, etc. publish one tiny package per platform whose entire purpose is shipping the corresponding binary. We suppress for these by name pattern, matched against the owning manifest's OWN declared name (data.name) — never against a dependency it declares.
